Eleven realistic defects have been injected into a copy of `CASE-SM`. Build the
checks, then grade yourself against the manifest.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

LLOQ = 1.0
raw = pd.read_csv("../../cases/case-sm/data/ozanib_pk_messy.csv", dtype={"ID": str})

print(f"{len(raw)} rows, {raw.ID.nunique()} subjects")
raw.head(4)
```

Note the `dtype={"ID": str}`. Reading identifiers as strings is a habit worth
forming: pandas will happily turn `007` into `7`, and then your merge silently
drops a subject.

## The battery

Each check appends to a findings list rather than raising, so one run reports
everything wrong at once. In production you would raise at the end if the list
is non-empty — a build that continues past a failed check is not a check.

```{python}
findings = []

def flag(code, msg, ids=()):
    findings.append(dict(code=code, message=msg,
                         ids=sorted(set(map(str, ids)))))
```

### C01 · Identifier format

```{python}
bad = [i for i in raw.ID.unique() if str(i) != str(int(float(i)))]
if bad:
    flag("ID_FORMAT", f"{len(bad)} ID(s) not in canonical numeric form", bad)
```

### C02 · Duplicate event keys

```{python}
key = ["ID", "TIME", "EVID", "CMT"]
d = raw[raw.duplicated(key, keep=False)]
if len(d):
    flag("DUP_RECORDS", f"{len(d)} rows share an (ID, TIME, EVID, CMT) key", d.ID.unique())
```

### C03 · Negative time

```{python}
d = raw[raw.TIME < 0]
if len(d):
    flag("NEGATIVE_TIME", f"{len(d)} record(s) with TIME < 0", d.ID.unique())
```

### C04 · Dose must sort before an observation at the same time

```{python}
bad = []
for i, g in raw.groupby("ID", sort=False):
    for t, gt in g.groupby("TIME"):
        if len(gt) > 1 and gt.EVID.iloc[0] == 0 and (gt.EVID == 1).any():
            bad.append(i)
if bad:
    flag("DOSE_ORDER", "observation sorts before the dose at the same TIME", bad)
```

### C05 · Regular dosing intervals

```{python}
bad = []
for i, g in raw.groupby("ID", sort=False):
    dt = np.sort(g.loc[g.EVID == 1, "TIME"].values)
    if len(dt) == 0:
        bad.append(i)
        continue
    gaps = np.diff(dt)
    if len(gaps) and (np.abs(gaps - np.median(gaps)) > 1e-6).any():
        bad.append(i)
if bad:
    flag("MISSING_DOSE", "irregular gap in the dosing sequence", bad)
```

### C06 · Zero used to mean missing

```{python}
d = raw[(raw.EVID == 0) & (raw.DV == 0)]
if len(d):
    flag("ZERO_MEANS_MISSING", f"{len(d)} observation(s) with DV exactly 0", d.ID.unique())
```

### C07 · BLQ consistency

```{python}
d = raw[(raw.EVID == 0) & raw.DV.notna() & (raw.DV < LLOQ) & (raw.BLQ == 0)]
if len(d):
    flag("BLQ_IMPUTED", f"{len(d)} value(s) below LLOQ not flagged BLQ", d.ID.unique())
```

### C08 · Unit switch

Compare each subject's late concentrations against their own early ones. A
within-subject comparison is far more sensitive than a population range check,
because it does not have to see through between-subject variability.

```{python}
o = raw[(raw.EVID == 0) & raw.DV.notna() & (raw.TIME > 0)]
bad = []
for i, g in o.groupby("ID", sort=False):
    early, late = g[g.TIME < 240].DV, g[g.TIME >= 240].DV
    if len(early) > 2 and len(late) > 0 and late.median() < early.median() / 100:
        bad.append(i)
if bad:
    flag("UNIT_SWITCH", "late concentrations >100x lower than early ones", bad)
```

### C09 · Covariate plausibility

```{python}
d = raw[(raw.WT < 35) | (raw.WT > 250)]
if len(d):
    flag("IMPOSSIBLE_COVARIATE", "body weight outside 35-250 kg", d.ID.unique())
```

### C10 · Baseline covariates constant within subject

```{python}
bad_cols = [c for c in ["AGE", "SEX", "WT", "DOSE"] if raw.groupby("ID")[c].nunique().max() > 1]
if bad_cols:
    ids = set()
    for c in bad_cols:
        n = raw.groupby("ID")[c].nunique()
        ids |= set(n[n > 1].index)
    flag("TIME_VARYING_BASELINE", f"baseline covariate(s) vary within subject: {bad_cols}", ids)
```

### C11 · Dose magnitude

```{python}
d = raw[(raw.EVID == 1) & ((raw.AMT < 1) | (raw.AMT > 1000))]
if len(d):
    flag("DOSE_UNIT", "AMT outside a plausible 1-1000 mg range", d.ID.unique())
```

## The report

```{python}
for f in findings:
    ids = ",".join(f["ids"][:6]) + ("..." if len(f["ids"]) > 6 else "")
    print(f"{f['code']:22s} {f['message']:55s} -> ID {ids}")
print(f"\n{len(findings)} check(s) failed")
```

## Grade yourself

```{python}
manifest = pd.read_csv("../../cases/case-sm/data/ozanib_pk_messy_manifest.csv")
found = {f["code"] for f in findings}
injected = set(manifest.code)

print(f"injected : {len(injected)}")
print(f"detected : {len(found & injected)}")
print(f"missed   : {sorted(injected - found) or 'none'}")
print(f"spurious : {sorted(found - injected) or 'none'}")
```

::: {.callout-important}
Look at which subjects trip **C07** (BLQ consistency). Subjects 11–14 appear
there as well as in **C08**, because dividing their concentrations by a thousand
pushed them below the LLOQ. One injected defect, two independent alarms.

That redundancy is the argument for running the whole battery rather than
stopping at the first failure — and for reading *which* subjects each check
names, not just how many checks failed.
:::

## Now fix them

Detection is half the job. Each defect has a different correct response, and
"correct" sometimes means *refuse to guess*.

```{python}
fixes = pd.DataFrame([
    ("ID_FORMAT",            "normalise in the assembly script, re-run every join"),
    ("DUP_RECORDS",          "de-duplicate on the event key AFTER confirming they are true duplicates"),
    ("NEGATIVE_TIME",        "decide the reference time; a screening sample may belong to a prior period"),
    ("DOSE_ORDER",           "re-sort ID, TIME, then EVID descending"),
    ("MISSING_DOSE",         "recover from source EX; if unrecoverable, exclude the interval and log it"),
    ("ZERO_MEANS_MISSING",   "set to NA with MDV = 1; never carry a 0 into a log-scale model"),
    ("BLQ_IMPUTED",          "restore the flag from the raw assay export; do not un-impute by arithmetic"),
    ("UNIT_SWITCH",          "confirm against the laboratory report, then convert once at the boundary"),
    ("IMPOSSIBLE_COVARIATE", "query the site; do not silently correct a decimal point"),
    ("TIME_VARYING_BASELINE","take the baseline visit value; check the join key"),
    ("DOSE_UNIT",            "confirm against source EX, then convert once"),
], columns=["code", "correct response"])

print(fixes.to_string(index=False))
```

Three of these — the missing dose, the impossible weight, the unit switch —
cannot be resolved inside the analysis at all. They require going back to
source. **A check that you "fix" by guessing has been converted from a defect
you know about into a defect you do not.**

## What to try next

1. Add a check that every subject has at least one observation after their last
   dose. What does it catch that nothing above does?
2. Make C08 more general: flag any subject whose residual variability against a
   naive pooled fit is an order of magnitude worse than the population median.
3. Turn the battery into a function that raises on any finding, and run it as a
   pre-commit hook. That is the version that actually protects you.
